Delaware law sets out when a person occupying land can claim title by adverse possession, and how an owner can remove someone who has no right to be there.

What the official sources say

  • 10 Del. C. 7901: no person may make entry into lands except within 20 years after the person's right or title first descended or accrued. (10 Del. C. Sec. 7901; source)
  • 10 Del. C. 7902: no action or claim of seisin unless actual seisin or possession within 20 years before the action. (10 Del. C. Sec. 7902; source)
  • 10 Del. C. 7903: a person who is an infant, mentally ill or imprisoned when the right accrues may enter or sue within 10 years after the disability is removed. (10 Del. C. Sec. 7903; source)

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Delaware statutes set the basic rules between landlords and tenants, including deposits, notices and what happens when a rental is sold.

What the official sources say

  • 25 Del. C. 5514(a): security deposit may not exceed 1 month's rent for leases of 1 year or more and for month-to-month tenancies lasting 1 year or more (excess must be credited back); limits do not apply to furnished units. (25 Del. C. Sec. 5514; source)
  • Landlord must remit the deposit and provide an itemized damage list within 20 days after termination or expiration; failure entitles tenant to double the amount wrongfully withheld (5514(e), (f)). (25 Del. C. Sec. 5514(e)-(f); source)
  • Retaliation prohibited (5516): eviction action, rent increase or service decrease after a good-faith code complaint, tenant organizing or pursuing legal remedies; presumed retaliatory if within 90 days. (25 Del. C. Sec. 5516; source)
  • Termination of a month-to-month tenancy: at least 60 days written notice, with the 60 days starting the first day of the month after actual notice (25 Del. C. 5106). (Delaware Courts Landlord/Tenant help page citing 25 Del. C. 5106; source)
Selling in Delaware?
We buy Delaware houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Can a Delaware landlord end a tenancy just because the house is being sold?

Not on that ground alone, as far as the code we reviewed shows. The grounds for summary possession in 25 Del. C. 5702 do not list a sale of the property, so an owner who wants a vacant house has to use the notice rules that apply to the tenancy.

Under 25 Del. C. 5106, a landlord may end a fixed-term agreement by giving at least 60 days' written notice before the term expires, stating that it ends on its expiration date. A month-to-month tenancy needs 60 days' written notice, counted from the first day of the month after actual notice. A written lease cannot run longer than one year unless the law says otherwise, and a lease with no stated term is treated as month-to-month.

If a lease runs a year or more and neither side gives notice at least 60 days before it ends (45 days for the tenant), section 5108 turns it into a month-to-month tenancy on the same terms. A seller who misses that window can end up with a tenant in place at closing.

How can a seller show a rental to buyers?

A landlord must give 48 hours' notice before entering and may enter only between 8:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m. That comes from 25 Del. C. 5509, and it covers showings as well as repairs.

  • The tenant may not unreasonably withhold consent for the landlord to exhibit the unit to prospective purchasers, mortgagees or tenants.
  • The 48-hour notice can be waived in a signed addendum or separate signed document for prospective tenants or purchasers only.
  • Emergencies allow entry at any time.
  • A landlord cannot use access to harass a tenant, and repeated unreasonable entry can be treated by the tenant as grounds to terminate.
  • Section 5510 makes the landlord liable for theft, casualty or other harm from entry made without the tenant's consent when the tenant is absent or present and able to consent.

Photos, lockbox visits and open houses all need to fit those limits. A cash buyer who inspects once, with notice, usually imposes less on a tenant than weeks of showings.

What happens to a tenant's retaliation protection during a sale?

Retaliation rules still apply, but a good-faith sale can be a defense. Section 5516 bars a landlord from seeking possession, raising rent or cutting services after a tenant makes a good-faith code complaint, organizes other tenants or pursues a legal remedy, and it presumes retaliation when the landlord acts within 90 days.

Paragraph (d)(7) gives a defense where the landlord has in good faith contracted to sell and the contract of sale contains a purchaser representation that the buyer will use the unit as the buyer's own residence, substantially alter or demolish it, or stop renting it for at least six months. A tenant who proves a violation can recover three months' rent or treble damages, whichever is greater, plus costs but excluding attorneys' fees.

Practical point: if a tenant made a repair complaint a few weeks ago, timing a notice around the sale invites a retaliation claim. Fix the complaint first, then plan the exit.

What notice must a landlord give for unpaid rent or a lease violation?

Seven days is the minimum in both cases. These are the steps in Chapter 55 and Chapter 57 of Title 25.

SituationNotice or stepSection
Unpaid rentWritten demand giving not less than 7 days before the landlord may file to terminate5502
Material lease breachWritten notice with at least 7 days to cure5513
Rent paid in full before filingLandlord may not file for possession on that ground5502(c)
Holdover after the term endsTenant owes up to double the monthly rent, prorated daily5515
Late feeCapped at 5 percent of monthly rent and not imposed within 5 days of the due date5501(d)

Section 5513 lets a landlord rely on the notice for a substantially similar breach within one year. Where a breach causes or threatens irreparable harm, the landlord may terminate on notice without the cure period.

How does an eviction case work in Delaware?

Possession cases go to the Justice of the Peace Court. Section 5701 puts an action for summary possession in the Justice of the Peace Court that hears civil cases in the county where the rental is located.

  • The landlord files a complaint for possession, and the court serves the complaint with a notice of the hearing time and place (section 5704).
  • Under section 5702A, after filing, the case is scheduled for mediation through the court's residential eviction diversion program. Mediation must be completed at least 48 hours before trial, and a tenant's failure to engage does not delay trial.
  • Section 5704A requires lead-based paint documentation with the complaint.
  • Notices must be served personally, left with an adult at the unit, or mailed, and posting works only when combined with a return receipt or certificate of mailing (section 5113).

The other grounds in section 5702 include holding over after the agreement ends, deducting wrongfully from rent, breaching a lawful obligation, holding over more than 5 days after a foreclosure sale with perfected title, and a sole tenant's death. Section 5115 allows an expedited forthwith summons where a tenant has caused substantial or irreparable harm.

Self-help is not an option. The Delaware code abolishes the landlord's right of distress for rent in section 5120, and a lease clause for attorneys' fees is unenforceable under section 5111.

What should a seller do about a tenant's belongings and keys?

If a landlord wins possession and there is no appeal, the landlord may remove and store the tenant's items at the tenant's expense. Seven days after the appeal period expires, the property is deemed abandoned and may be disposed of without further notice or liability (section 5507(e)).

Section 5125 covers keys. A lease cannot require surrender before the end of the term, and where there is more than one tenant possession is returned only when all of them have complied. Document everything with photos, dates and written notices.

On the money side, a landlord who sells should know that a tenant's surety bond travels with the lease. Under section 5514A(j), if the landlord's interest is sold or transferred, the new landlord must accept the tenant's surety bond and may not demand an additional security deposit during the current term.

What does the Delaware rental market look like for owners?

Delaware has about 402,000 households and a statewide median gross rent of $1,401. Rentals are a minority, since about 73% of occupied homes are owner-occupied.

MeasureDelaware
Households, 2020 to 2024402,038
Owner-occupied housing unit rate73.0%
Median gross rent$1,401
Median owner costs with a mortgage, monthly$1,816

Source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts. Rules shift over time. Several sections, including 5102 and 5512, have versions that take effect March 8, 2027, and the source-of-income fair housing rules in section 5116 have a different version effective December 31, 2028. Check the current text before you act.

When a rental becomes a burden, a cash buyer can purchase the house with the tenant in place or after the tenant leaves, on terms you negotiate. We are not attorneys, so have counsel review notices and the lease first.

More questions about Delaware Landlord Tenant Law and Tenant Rights

How much notice must a Delaware landlord give to end a month-to-month tenancy?

At least 60 days in writing, counted from the first day of the month after actual notice, under 25 Del. C. 5106(d). The tenant gives the same notice to end it.

How much notice does a landlord need to enter to show a rental?

At least 48 hours, and entry is allowed only between 8:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m. under 25 Del. C. 5509. Emergencies are the exception, and a tenant can sign a waiver of the 48 hours for prospective purchasers.

Where are Delaware eviction cases filed?

In the Justice of the Peace Court that hears civil cases for the county where the rental sits. After filing, the case is scheduled for mediation before trial.

Can a tenant stay if the landlord sells the house?

The sale is not listed as a ground for summary possession, so the landlord still has to end the tenancy through the lease terms and the notice rules. A buyer should ask for the lease and any notices before closing.

What if a tenant stays after the lease ends?

The tenant owes up to double the monthly rent, prorated daily, for each day of holdover under section 5515. The landlord must still use the court process to regain possession.
